questions.question: If a person has undamaged eardrums and ear bones, but the specialized sensory hair cells inside their cochlea are destroyed, what will occur when sound waves enter the ear canal?
options: Vibrations reach the cochlea, but electrical signals are not generated to be sent along the nerve
No vibrations occur at the eardrum because the cochlea controls eardrum movement
Sound signals travel directly to the brain via air pressure rather than nerves
The brain receives electrical signals but misinterprets them as visual light signals

questions.question: A patient's ear structures, cochlea, and auditory nerve are all functioning normally, but a brain injury damages the specific area responsible for processing auditory nerve impulses. What will be the outcome?
options: The brain creates an exaggerated sensation of extremely loud sound continuously
Vibrations occur in the ear, but the patient experiences no sensation of hearing sound
The sound waves are reflected back out of the ear without causing any ear bones to vibrate
The nerve sends vibrations directly back to the eardrum, producing an internal echo

questions.question: Four sound waves with equal energy are played in a quiet room: Wave A (15 Hz), Wave B (3000 Hz), Wave C (15000 Hz), Wave D (25000 Hz). Which sound wave will a human ear detect with the greatest sensitivity?
options: Wave A
Wave B
Wave C
Wave D

questions.question: An acoustic signal has a frequency of 12 Hz, and another signal has a frequency of 30000 Hz. How are these two signals categorized, and can normal human ears hear them?
options: 12 Hz is ultrasound and 30000 Hz is infrasound; neither can be heard by human ears
12 Hz is infrasound and 30000 Hz is ultrasound; both can be heard by human ears
12 Hz is infrasound and 30000 Hz is ultrasound; neither can be heard by human ears
12 Hz is infrasound and 30000 Hz is ultrasound; only 12 Hz can be heard by human ears

questions.question: A loudspeaker playing a steady tone is placed near a suspended dust particle in air. Describe the motion of the dust particle as the sound wave travels past it towards a wall.
options: The dust particle travels continuously forward alongside the sound wave until it hits the wall
The dust particle moves back and forth parallel to the direction the sound is travelling, remaining in the same average location
The dust particle moves up and down at 90 degrees to the direction the sound is travelling
The dust particle remains completely motionless while air molecules flow past it to the wall

questions.question: Which statement correctly explains why sound is classified as a longitudinal wave rather than a transverse wave?
options: Sound requires a medium to travel, whereas transverse waves do not require any medium
Particles vibrate perpendicular to the direction in which energy is transferred
Sound waves can travel through a vacuum at high speed
The direction of particle vibration is parallel to the direction of energy transfer

questions.question: Why does sound travel noticeably faster through liquid water than through air?
options: Air particles are much closer together, so they absorb the sound energy before it can travel far
Water particles are much closer together than air particles, enabling vibrations to pass from particle to particle more quickly
Water particles are heavier and travel long distances carrying the sound wave across the liquid
Liquid water creates lower friction against the sound wave than air does

questions.question: Comparing a sound wave travelling through a solid steel rod to one travelling through liquid water, why does the sound wave travel faster in the steel rod?
options: Steel has stronger forces between its particles than water, allowing vibrations to spread even faster
Particles in steel move freely across the length of the rod carrying energy faster than liquid particles
Water particles have no forces between them, which slows down the transmission of sound vibrations
Sound waves travel as transverse waves in steel but as light waves in water

questions.question: Sound pulses are produced simultaneously at one end of three identical 1 km pipes containing air, water, and iron respectively. In what order will the sound pulses arrive at the far end of the pipes?
options: Air pipe first, then water pipe, then iron pipe
Water pipe first, then iron pipe, then air pipe
Iron pipe first, then water pipe, then air pipe
All three pulses will arrive at the exact same time

questions.question: A sound wave travels a distance of 1020 meters through air in 3 seconds. What is the calculated speed of sound in this experiment?
A climber claps their hands in front of a tall vertical cliff wall and hears an echo 2 seconds later. If the speed of sound in air is 340 m/s, how far away is the cliff from the climber?

Two students measure the speed of sound in air using clappers and a stopwatch. Group A measures sound travelling over 20 metres, while Group B measures sound travelling over 300 metres. Why is Group B's result likely to be more reliable?
options: Sound travels faster over 300 metres than over 20 metres
Measuring a longer time interval reduces human reaction time error as a proportion of the total measured time
Over longer distances, sound waves change from longitudinal to transverse waves
Group B does not need to use a timing device because long distances eliminate all experimental errors

questions.question: A device emits a sound wave with a frequency of 25000 Hz. Why is this wave classified as ultrasound?
options: Its frequency is below the lower threshold of human hearing (20 Hz)
Its speed is faster than the speed of light in a vacuum
Its frequency is above 20000 Hz, which is beyond the upper limit of human hearing
It is a transverse electromagnetic wave rather than a mechanical wave

questions.question: Which pair of statements correctly describes key properties of ultrasound waves when used in medical scanning?
options: They transfer energy by causing vibrations, and they do not cause harm to the human body
They carry no energy, but they can burn body tissues if applied for more than a second
They travel only through a vacuum, making them safe for inner body imaging
They destroy cell DNA like X-rays, but cause no physical vibrations in tissue

questions.question: How does ultrasound technology construct a clear image of an unborn baby inside a mother's womb?
options: Ultrasound waves pass straight through all tissues without stopping, projecting a shadow on a film behind the mother
Ultrasound waves are absorbed completely by skin, producing heat signals that the computer converts to images
Ultrasound waves reflect at boundaries between different types of tissues, and these returning signals are detected to form an image
Ultrasound waves turn into light waves when they encounter body fluids, illuminating the inside of the womb

questions.question: Which of the following describes two valid non-imaging applications of high-frequency ultrasound waves?
options: Generating electricity in solar cells and heating drinking water in homes
Cleaning intricate delicate jewelry items and helping to treat muscle injuries in physiotherapy
Magnetising metals in factories and sterilising air inside vacuum chambers
Increasing the speed of sound in air and changing the frequency of human speech

questions.question: A plastic duck is floating on a calm pond when water ripples pass underneath it. What will happen to the plastic duck as the wave passes?
options: The duck will travel across the pond in the exact direction the wave is travelling
The duck will bob up and down in place, moving vertically rather than travelling forward with the wave
The duck will sink to the bottom of the pond because waves push objects downwards
The duck will move sideways at 180 degrees opposite to the direction of wave travel

questions.question: A ripple moves horizontally across the surface of a pond from left to right. What is the direction of oscillation of the water particles forming this wave?
options: Horizontally from left to right, parallel to energy transfer
Vertically up and down, at 90 degrees to the direction of energy transfer
In circles travelling forward along with the energy transfer
Horizontally from right to left, opposite to energy transfer

questions.question: Two identical water wave crests meet each other while travelling in opposite directions across a tank. What phenomenon occurs at the point where they overlap?
options: Reflection: the two waves turn into sound waves and bounce away
Refraction: the waves slow down to zero speed permanently
Superposition: the two wave crests combine to produce a single larger wave height at that moment
Absorption: the waves disappear completely and create a vacuum in the water

questions.question: When a sound wave reaches the ear, what sequence of vibrations occurs inside the ear before an electrical signal is generated?
options: The cochlea vibrates first, passing vibrations to the tiny bones and then to the eardrum.
The eardrum vibrates first, passing vibrations to the tiny bones, which then cause the cochlea to vibrate.
The auditory nerve vibrates first, passing vibrations through the tiny bones to the eardrum.
The tiny bones vibrate first in response to air pressure, causing the eardrum and cochlea to vibrate simultaneously.

questions.question: A person hears a musical note. Which component of the ear detects the physical vibrations and causes electrical signals to be sent along a nerve?
options: Specialised cells inside the cochlea
The outer membrane of the eardrum
The fluid inside the semicircular canals
The three tiny bones in the middle ear

questions.question: A person's outer and inner ear structures are completely healthy and vibrate normally, but their nerve connecting the ear to the brain is damaged. What will happen?
options: The person will hear sounds at a much higher pitch than usual.
The person will not experience the sensation of hearing because signals cannot reach the brain.
The brain will create sound sensations directly from the eardrum vibrations without nerve signals.
The person will hear an echo of every sound with a delay.

questions.question: An audio engineer tests human hearing with different sound wave frequencies. Which frequency wave is the human ear most sensitive to?
options: 15 Hz
500 Hz

questions.question: When a loudspeaker cone vibrates back and forth, how does it transmit sound through the surrounding air?
options: It pushes air particles so they stream continuously from the speaker to the listener's ear.
It causes nearby air particles to vibrate back and forth, passing vibrations to neighboring air particles.
It creates light-like radiation that travels through empty space between air molecules.
It heats the air particles, causing them to rise rapidly and carry sound upward.

questions.question: A scientist tracks a single air particle while a sound wave travels horizontally from left to right through a room. What is the motion of this air particle?
options: It moves continuously from left to right across the room alongside the sound wave.
It vibrates back and forth horizontally, parallel to the direction of wave travel.
It moves in a circle perpendicular to the direction of wave travel.
It moves up and down vertically at 90 degrees to the direction of wave travel.

questions.question: Why is sound classified as a longitudinal wave rather than a transverse wave?
options: Because sound waves can travel through a vacuum without any particles present.
Because the direction of particle vibration is parallel to the direction of energy transfer.
Because the direction of particle vibration is at a right angle (90°) to the direction of energy transfer.
Because sound waves travel faster than transverse waves in all materials.

questions.question: Sound travels faster through water (a liquid) than through air (a gas). What particle explanation accounts for this difference?
options: Liquid particles are much closer together than gas particles, so vibrations are easily passed on.
Liquid particles travel across long distances much faster than gas particles can move.
Liquid particles have larger amplitude vibrations than gas particles when hit by sound waves.
Gas particles attract each other much more strongly than liquid particles do.

questions.question: Why does a sound wave travel faster through a solid steel rod than through liquid water?
options: Solid particles move freely past each other, carrying sound energy forward rapidly.
Solids contain large gaps between particles, giving sound room to accelerate.
The strong forces between particles in solids allow vibrations to travel even faster.
Steel particles have less mass than water particles, so they vibrate at higher frequencies.

questions.question: Compare the speed of sound across three media: air (gas), water (liquid), and steel (solid). Which option correctly lists the speed of sound from slowest to fastest?
options: Air (slowest), Water, Steel (fastest)
Steel (slowest), Water, Air (fastest)
Water (slowest), Air, Steel (fastest)
Air (slowest), Steel, Water (fastest)

questions.question: A student stands in front of a tall, hard concrete wall and claps loudly. A short time later, she hears the clap again. What wave behavior causes this echo?
options: Refraction of sound as it changes speed inside the wall
Superposition of sound waves absorbing into the concrete surface
Sound waves reflecting from the hard surface and traveling back
Diffraction of sound waves bending around the edges of the wall

questions.question: A sonar system sends a sound pulse down through seawater to the ocean bed. If the sound travels a distance of 3000 meters in 2 seconds, what is the speed of sound in this water?

Two groups of students measure the speed of sound outdoors. Group A measures over a distance of 10 meters, while Group B measures over 300 meters. Why is Group B's method likely to yield a more accurate speed calculation?
options: Sound waves travel faster when moving across longer distances.
Measuring longer distances and times means measurement errors are a smaller proportion of the values.
Air particles only vibrate properly when sound travels more than 50 meters.
Measuring over 300 meters removes the need to use a stopwatch.

questions.question: A signal generator emits a sound wave with a frequency of 25 000 Hz. Why can a human standing nearby not hear this sound?
options: The frequency is below 20 Hz, which is infrasound.
The frequency is above 20 000 Hz, which is ultrasound.
Sound waves above 20 000 Hz cannot travel through air.
The wave becomes a transverse wave at high frequencies.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a physical property and safety aspect of ultrasound waves used in body scans?
options: Ultrasound waves cause objects to vibrate and transfer energy, but do not cause harm to the human body.
Ultrasound waves carry no energy, making them safe for human tissue.
Ultrasound waves cause harmful ionizing radiation in human cells.
Ultrasound waves stop all cellular vibrations upon entering body tissues.

questions.question: How can ultrasound be used to produce detailed images of structures inside the human body?
options: By measuring the heat generated when ultrasound passes through tissues.
By detecting ultrasound waves that reflect back from boundaries between different tissues.
By turning ultrasound waves into visible light beams inside internal organs.
By forcing organs to release magnetic signals picked up by external sensors.

questions.question: Beyond medical imaging, which pair of applications relies on the energy transfer and vibrations of ultrasound?
options: Magnetizing metals and lighting electric bulbs
Cleaning delicate objects and treating injuries in physiotherapy
Freezing liquids rapidly and measuring air pressure
Generating electricity in solar panels and heating rooms

questions.question: A toy rubber duck floats on a pond. A ripple passes under the duck moving from left to right. How does the duck move as the wave passes?
options: It travels continuously to the right edge of the pond with the wave.
It moves up and down in place (oscillates) without moving forward.
It sinks to the bottom of the pond permanently.
It moves to the left, opposite to the wave direction.

questions.question: Why are water surface waves classified as transverse waves?
options: The direction of water oscillation is parallel to the direction of wave energy transfer.
The direction of water oscillation is 90° to the direction of wave energy transfer.
Water particles travel forward at the same speed as the energy.
Water waves can travel through empty space without particles.

questions.question: Two sets of water waves meet in a ripple tank. At a specific point, the crest of one wave coincides with the trough of another wave, resulting in flat water for an instant. What term describes this interaction?
options: Reflection
Wave superposition
Refraction
Echo formation
